# ThinkFLOW

> Fixed-fee cloud cost audits, website creation and care, short-form clipping and Python automation, run by Daniel Burcea from Bucharest, Romania. Real case study behind the audit offer: our own AI inference stack migrated off AWS, $2,745/mo down to $377/mo (86%), with P95 latency improved from 310 ms to 145 ms — full methodology published.

## Services

- [Cloud Cost & Migration Audit](https://thinkflow.ro/services/cloud-cost-migration-audit): fixed EUR 1,500-4,000, line-item AWS/GPU bill review plus a benchmarked migration plan; no percentage-of-savings clauses.
- [Website Creation & Care](https://thinkflow.ro/services/website-care): site builds from EUR 1,500; monthly care plans (updates with prior backups, restore-tested backups, daily monitoring, plain-language reports) from 300 RON/month for the Romanian market.
- [Short-Form Clipping](https://thinkflow.ro/services/clipping): ready-to-post clips from long episodes; Pilot $75 one-time (3 clips), plans from $290/month; first sample batch free.
- [Python Automation](https://thinkflow.ro/services/python-automation): scrapers, API integrations, data pipelines, EUR 50-500 per job.
- [AI Voice Agent](https://thinkflow.ro/services/ai-voice-agent): phone agent in natural Romanian — in development, early-access waitlist open.

## Key resources

- [The 2026 Cloud Exit Guide: AWS to Hetzner GPU](https://thinkflow.ro/blog/2026-cloud-exit-guide-aws-hetzner): the published case study behind the audit numbers — cost tables, latency benchmarks, phased migration plan.
- [WordPress maintenance: what it includes and costs in 2026](https://thinkflow.ro/blog/mentenanta-site-wordpress-2026): what a serious care plan contains and market pricing.
- [Free site health report](https://thinkflow.ro/raport-site): passive technical check (mobile speed, SSL, visible issues), delivered by email within 24 working hours, no passwords requested.
- [Blog](https://thinkflow.ro/blog): technical articles with original benchmarks on AI infrastructure, cloud hosting and web development.
